subject: MAP: performance benchmarking & HW sizing proposal for LogiCloud evaluation
messages:

Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP kickoff — perf goals & initial constraints

Karthik / team,

Thanks for the draft MAP in our call this morning. To make the evaluation productive we need a short, executable perf plan we can run in our staging account this week. High-level goals from our side:

- Target production-like load: 8 concurrent sessions, 300ms p95 latency target for interactive chat (TTFT budget 150ms).
- Throughput: sustained 200 tokens/sec across the fleet for background batch jobs.
- Cost sensitivity: prefer recommendations that balance latency and unit cost; LogiCloud is open to a mixed fleet approach.

Can you send a concrete list of test cases, hardware permutations (A100/H100/L40S, MIG vs full), and expected sample metrics so we can sign off on the MAP and schedule the pilot?

Also please include a clear close timeline — we have quarter-end procurement constraints and would like decision + PO within 3 weeks if the results are positive.

Best,
Anna

--
Anna Petrova
Head of Platform Engineering, LogiCloud
anna@logicloud.com

Anna — thanks, this is helpful. Attached is a concise MAP + perf test plan (redwood_MAP_v1.2.pdf and perf_test_plan.csv). Key items included:

1) Test matrix:
   - Models: open-llama-70B (fp16), redwood-chat-3b (quantized) as lower-bound comparison.
   - GPUs: A100 40GB (full), H100 80GB (full), L40S 48GB (full), and MIG slices (e.g., 1g.10g equivalents on A100/H100 where applicable).
   - Workloads: interactive chat (avg 32 tokens per turn), long-form generation (512-token completions), embedding bulk jobs (batch size up to 1024).

2) Metrics we will capture: TTFT, p50/p90/p95 latency (token and request-level), tokens/sec per GPU, memory utilization, GPU SM utilization, and cost estimate per 1M tokens.

3) Sizing guidance: we will produce a recommendation matrix for low-latency endpoints (pin to H100 / dedicated small pool) vs high-throughput batch (L40S or A100 with larger batch sizes).

4) Timeline & milestones:
   - Perf runbook delivery: today
   - Test execution (Redwood SE + LogiCloud): 21–23 Jul
   - Preliminary results: 24 Jul
   - MAP finalization + SOW draft: 26 Jul

Monica — can you lead the perf runs and capture the artifact CSV? Laura, I’ll need approval to propose the pilot config in the SOW for 3 H100 nodes + 5 L40S nodes as a starting point.

Anna — we added expected sample outputs in the CSV so you can see how we’ll present p95 vs concurrency curves. If this looks good I’ll schedule the test window for later today.

Thanks,
Karthik

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 24 Jul 2026 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — perf goals & initial constraints

Anna / Karthik — preliminary results attached (map_perftest_results_20260724.csv and latency_throughput_summary_20260724.pdf). Highlights and sizing recommendations below — caveats at the end.

Summary (interactive chat workload, model: open-llama-70B fp16, average 32 tokens per request):
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) median: H100 full = 52ms, A100 full = 92ms, L40S = 60ms. Network add ~12–18ms in staging.
- p95 request-level latency at concurrency=8: H100 full = 180ms, A100 full = 320ms, L40S = 210ms.
- Sustained tokens/sec per full GPU (512-token workload): H100 ~9.8k toks/sec, A100 ~6.1k toks/sec, L40S ~8.5k toks/sec.
- MIG slices (approx 1/4 of full): throughput drops ~3.6x vs full GPU for this model due to reduced SMs and memory; per-slice p95 increases by ~1.8x under concurrency.

Sizing recommendations (to meet LogiCloud target: p95 <= 300ms; preferred p95 <= 200ms at concurrency=8):
- Low-latency interactive endpoints: allocate H100 full GPUs (3 nodes, 1 model replica each) — gives headroom for autoscale and keeps p95 ~180ms at concurrency 8.
- Cost-sensitive mixed workloads: L40S is a good middle ground; 5 L40S nodes provide ~85% of H100 throughput at ~70–80% of H100 cost in our pricing model; p95 at concurrency 8 ~210ms.
- High-throughput batch jobs: use A100 full or L40S with higher batch sizes (batch 16–32) — tokens/sec improves >2x for batch workloads compared to interactive configs.
- MIG for multi-tenant smaller endpoints: workable for background inference but not recommended for primary interactive endpoints due to higher p95 and lower TTFT headroom. Consider MIG for embedding microservices to increase density.

Cost note (rough): to meet the interactive SLA at 8 concurrent sessions, estimated monthly infra run-rate (pilot scale)
- 3x H100 nodes: ~$XXk/mo (approx relative baseline)
- 5x L40S nodes: ~$YYk/mo (lower)
Exact quotes will be in SOW.

Caveats:
- These runs were on staging H100s with slightly different kernel tuning than Redwood-hosted infra; Rishi is capturing the kernel flags. We expect a modest ~5–10% variance when moving to Redwood-managed runtime with optimized kernels.
- Long-tail latency can be sensitive to tokenization spikes (we saw p99 spikes when responses exceeded 256 tokens).

Next steps:
- Karthik: propose pilot SOW with 3 H100 + 5 L40S as discussed; include 2-week ramp and performance acceptance criteria (p95 <= 220ms at concurrency 8).
- Anna: confirm if we should include MIG-based embedding service in the PO as a lower-cost add-on.
- Rishi: attach kernel/compilation notes and final CSV to the MAP.

Attachments: map_perftest_results_20260724.csv, latency_throughput_summary_20260724.pdf

Thanks,
Monica
